notes.head: Clear path is not a claim that it is easy
notes.body: It says the behaviour survives and the route is known. A quote template rebuilt from scratch is a clear path — the finished document is reproducible and every part of it has a destination. Shape is where the work shows: Fan-out means one construct becomes several records, Rebuild means it is authored fresh rather than imported.

notes.head: Ramp pricing has hard edges, and a route around them
notes.body: A ramp needs at least two periods, applies only to recurring lines, and cannot be applied to a bundle header or an option product. Stepped periods on a bundled product are still buildable with Update Bundle Members rules — what is lost is the native grouping, period badges and MRR handling. Quantity is also locked across ramp periods, which is the most common reason a segmented subscription lands on Degraded.

notes.head: Dated conversion rates: quoting carries, authoring does not
notes.body: HubSpot holds one current rate per currency, set manually or updated on a schedule from Open Exchange Rates. A deal's rate is stamped at close and history stays viewable, so point-in-time quoting carries. What does not carry is authoring a rate against a named past or future period. 1 of your currencies maintain more than one rate period, which is the practice that does not reproduce.

notes.head: The formula limits are specific
notes.body: Calculated pricing supports IF, CASE, AND, OR, NOT, ISBLANK, BLANKVALUE, MIN and MAX — and AND / OR take two to five arguments each. A price action that ANDs six conditions is over the limit even though every function it uses is supported. The report prints the specific limit each formula breaches.

notes.head: Contracted pricing states its cardinality
notes.body: It lands as a price book assigned to a company, which also locks the quote so reps cannot switch away from negotiated pricing. Your 3 contracted prices across 2 accounts become 2 price books and 3 entries, expressed as import file rows.

notes.head: Discount tiers are half-open
notes.body: CPQ validates that each tier lower bound equals the previous upper bound, so a schedule reads 1–5, 5–10, 10–25. Reading those as inclusive ranges shifts every boundary by one unit and misprices the tier edges, so the convention is preserved on import.

notes.head: Package-owned records are excluded everywhere
notes.body: CPQ ships its own metadata and configuration records into every org. Counted naively they become your customisation. Namespaced components are filtered on namespace; seeded configuration records are identified by an install signature. In this org: 2 SBQQ__CustomAction__c shipped with CPQ and were not counted.

notes.head: Apex classes and Flows were not scanned
notes.body: Neither can be attributed to a CPQ object reliably — matching strings in a class body over-matches on incidental references and under-matches on dynamic SOQL. Logic may exist there that this report does not see.

notes.head: Custom condition logic that does not parse
notes.body: 1 rule carry a Custom conditions-met expression the tool could not resolve against the conditions on the rule: Broken custom logic (references conditions 4 that do not exist). Those rules are counted under their type but their logic needs a look.
